name: Tezepelumab

discovery.note: Fully human IgG2λ antibody against thymic stromal lymphopoietin, co-developed with AstraZeneca. Year of the first published clinical study of the antibody (as AMG 157; Gauvreau et al., NEJM 2014).

tagline: First biologic blocking epithelial TSLP, for severe asthma without phenotype limits
summary: Tezepelumab is a human monoclonal antibody that blocks thymic stromal lymphopoietin (TSLP), an epithelial alarmin at the top of the airway inflammatory cascade. It is approved as add-on maintenance for severe asthma regardless of eosinophil count or allergic status.
mechanism: TSLP is released by airway epithelial cells in response to allergens, viruses, pollutants and injury, and activates dendritic cells, mast cells, ILC2s and T cells, driving both type 2 and non-type 2 inflammation.
Tezepelumab binds TSLP and prevents it from binding its receptor complex, lowering blood eosinophils, IgE, FeNO and IL-5/IL-13 levels and reducing airway hyperresponsiveness.
uses: Add-on maintenance therapy for severe asthma in patients aged 12 years and older

history.title: Amgen–AstraZeneca collaboration
history.detail: The two companies agree to co-develop five inflammation antibodies, including tezepelumab.

history.title: PATHWAY
history.detail: Phase 2 results show fewer asthma exacerbations, including in low-eosinophil patients.

history.title: NAVIGATOR
history.detail: Phase 3 results show reduced exacerbations across phenotypes.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in December for severe asthma, without a biomarker restriction.

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: Approved in the European Union in September.

pk.metabolism: Proteolytic catabolism to peptides and amino acids (no CYP metabolism)
pk.excretion: Not renally excreted as intact antibody; cleared by catabolism and target-mediated uptake

facts: It was the first asthma biologic approved without a requirement for an eosinophilic or allergic phenotype.
TSLP was originally identified as a growth factor produced by thymic stromal cells.

references.title: Gauvreau GM et al. Effects of an anti-TSLP antibody (NEJM 2014)
